objective: The model bake-off: DCLab's studio engine as it is against FLAML's AutoML on the same rows, holdout, training folds and metric; per dataset the holdout score with its interval, minutes and peak memory. The rule below decides package 34.8 and was fixed before the first run.

rule.decides: package 34.8: FLAML as one more family in the engine's models stage
rule.arm: flaml (FLAML's AutoML on the engine's prepared table and training folds, the time budget below)
rule.statistic: per dataset, a paired bootstrap of the holdout difference on the same holdout rows (2000 draws, whole groups when the split is grouped, rows otherwise), oriented so that a positive difference means FLAML scored better on the dataset's primary metric; the 95% percentile interval
rule.ahead: FLAML is ahead on a dataset when the interval's lower end is above 0
rule.behind: FLAML is behind on a dataset when the interval's upper end is below 0
rule.go: 34.8 goes ahead when FLAML is ahead on at least a third of the datasets where both engines finished (rounded up), and ahead on more datasets than it is behind

not_judged.ecommerce_clothing_reviews: FLAML sees no text (the engine's text recipe is DCLab's), while 34.8 would give FLAML the recipe's features: reported, never counted

rule.failures: a dataset where FLAML failed after its retry counts as FLAML behind; one where only DCLab failed is left out and listed in the decision; the decision is written only when every dataset was compared or failed after its retry
rule.too_few: fewer than 10 datasets judged: undecided, 34.8 waits
rule.time_and_memory: reported beside the scores, never in the rule

left_out.hyperack: known leaks (the final fares); the brief allows it only with its leaks removed, in a later version
left_out.bike_sharing_daily: a daily time series: the engine derives past-only lags that a tabular search has no equal of; not one of the expansion samples the brief names (imbalanced fraud, multiclass, text plus tabular)

protocol.holdout: the studio engine's locked holdout (20%: the latest rows under a time split, unseen groups under a group split, stratified random otherwise), read once by each engine
protocol.folds: the engine's training folds (bundle.cv_splits): FLAML searches on the same folds through a fixed splitter
protocol.rows: the engine's own sample (at most 20,000 rows, label-independent, its seed): both engines see the same rows
protocol.metric: the engine's primary metric for the dataset (its kind's default), both scored by the same function
protocol.intervals: each engine: the engine's own bootstrap (400 draws, 95%, clustered when grouped); the difference: paired bootstrap, 2000 draws
protocol.time_and_memory: wall minutes and the process's peak resident memory, each engine in its own process
protocol.engine_budget: the engine has no time knob: it runs as it is and its minutes are measured

limits: One holdout per dataset: one draw of the data, not a distribution over datasets.
FLAML gets the engine's raw tabular columns, not its engineered features or its text recipe: on the text dataset it sees no text.
Measured on an 8 GB MacBook Air with a five-minute FLAML budget; a longer budget or AutoGluon (later, on the M1 Max) may change the result.
Never a production approval: a benchmark result alone says nothing about deployment.
